arxiv-1809-01898.title: Propheticus: Generalizable Machine Learning Framework Internal Report
arxiv-1809-01898.creator: João R. Campos, Marco Vieira, Ernesto Costa
arxiv-1809-01898.description: Abstract Due to recent technological developments, Machine Learning (ML) , a subfield of Artificial Intelligence (AI) , has been successfully used to process and extract knowledge from a variety of complex problems. However, a thorough ML approach is complex and highly dependent on the problem at hand.

arxiv-2102-04111.title: The Newton polyhedron and positivity of F 3 2 {}_{2}F_{3} hypergeometric functions
arxiv-2102-04111.creator: Yong-Kum Cho, Seok-Young Chung
arxiv-2102-04111.description: Abstract Abstract. As for the {}_{2}F_{3} hypergeometric function of the form {}_{2}F_{3}\left[\begin{array}[]{c}a_{1},a_{2}\\ b_{1},b_{2},b_{3}\end{array}\biggr|-x^{2}\right]\hskip 18.49988pt(x>0), where all of parameters are assumed to be positive, we give sufficient conditions on (b_{1},b_{2},b_{3}) for its positivity in terms of Newton polyhedra with vertices consisting of permutations of \,(a_{2},a_{1}+1/2,2a_{1})\, or \,(a_{1},a_{2}+1/2,2a_{2}).

arxiv-2112-14030.title: Bipartite Graph Matching Algorithms for Clean-Clean Entity Resolution: An Empirical Evaluation
arxiv-2112-14030.creator: George Papadakis 1 , Vasilis Efthymiou 2 , Emmanouil Thanos 3 , Oktie Hassanzadeh 4
arxiv-2112-14030.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by George Papadakis 1 , Vasilis Efthymiou 2 , Emmanouil Thanos 3 , Oktie Hassanzadeh 4. Entity Resolution (ER) is the task of finding records that refer to the same real-world entities. A common scenario is when entities across two clean sources need to be resolved, which we refer to as Clean-Clean ER.

arxiv-2205-05880.title: Deep Decomposition and Bilinear Pooling Network for Blind Night-Time Image Quality Evaluation
arxiv-2205-05880.creator: Qiuping Jiang, Jiawu Xu, Yudong Mao, Wei Zhou, Xiongkuo Min, Guangtao Zhai
arxiv-2205-05880.description: Abstract Blind image quality assessment (BIQA), which aims to accurately predict the image quality without any pristine reference information, has been extensively concerned in the past decades. Especially, with the help of deep neural networks, great progress has been achieved.

arxiv-2305-03652.creator: Yang Liu 1,2,∗,† , Zheru Qiu 1,2,∗ , Xinru Ji 1,2 , Andrea Bancora 1,2 , Grigory Lihachev 1,2 , Johann Riemensberger 1,2 , Rui Ning Wang 1,2 , Andrey Voloshin 1,2 , and Tobias J. Kippenberg 1,2,‡
arxiv-2305-03652.description: Abstract Erbium-doped fiber lasers Barnes et al. 1989 ; Suzuki et al. 1989 ; Chow et al. 1996 exhibit high coherence and low noise as required for applications in fiber optic sensing Zadok et al. 2012 , gyroscopes, LiDAR, and optical frequency metrology Xu and Wise 2013 .

arxiv-2501-09630.title: Chern-Simons gravitational term coupled to a spectator field
arxiv-2501-09630.creator: Giorgio Orlando
arxiv-2501-09630.description: Abstract The Chern-Simons gravitational term is typically coupled to the inflaton field during inflation. In this work, we explore an alternative scenario where the Chern-Simons term is minimally coupled to a massive spectator field, σ \sigma , within a multi-field inflationary framework where the spectator field is linearly coupled to the inflaton.

arxiv-2502-20346.title: Equilibria and Learning in Modular Marketplaces
arxiv-2502-20346.creator: Kshipra Bhawalkar, Jeff Dean, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Neel Patel
arxiv-2502-20346.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kshipra Bhawalkar, Jeff Dean, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Neel Patel. We envision a marketplace where diverse entities offer specialized “modules” through APIs, allowing users to compose the outputs of these modules for complex tasks within a given budget. This paper studies the market design problem in such an ecosystem, where module owners strategically set prices for their APIs (to maximize their profit) and a central platform orchestrates the aggregation of module outputs at query-time.

arxiv-2509-15411.title: Enhancing Physical Layer Security in IoT-Based RF-FSO Integrated Networks: Multi-RIS Structures and their Impact on Secure Communication
arxiv-2509-15411.creator: Anika Tabassum Biva, Md. Ibrahim, A. S. M. Badrudduza, Imran Shafique Ansari
arxiv-2509-15411.description: Abstract Abstract Due to their ability to dynamically control the propagation environment, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) offer a promising solution to address the challenges of 6 6 G wireless communication, especially in the context of Internet of Things (IoT) networks.

arxiv-2510-04914.title: High-Energy Evolution of Power-Suppressed Amplitudes Preprint: ALBERTA-THY-3-25, CERN-TH-2025-190, TUM-HEP-1574/25
arxiv-2510-04914.creator: Maximilian Delto, Alexander Penin, Lorenzo Tancredi
arxiv-2510-04914.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Maximilian Delto, Alexander Penin, Lorenzo Tancredi. We present a new class of evolution equations which govern the high-energy behavior of power-suppressed scattering amplitudes. The equations can be viewed as a renormalization group flow with respect to the relevant effective field theory cutoff. A distinct feature of the method is in the use of a multidimensional cutoff to separate the relevant scales in problems characterized by a complex factorization structure.

arxiv-2510-05966.title: Eigenstructure of the linearized electrical impedance tomography problem under radial perturbations
arxiv-2510-05966.creator: Markus Hirvensalo
arxiv-2510-05966.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Markus Hirvensalo. We analyze the Fréchet derivative F F , that maps a perturbation in conductivity to the linearized change in boundary measurements governed by the conductivity equation. The domain is taken to be the unit ball B ⊂ ℝ d B\subset\mathbb{R}^{d} with d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 , and we choose perturbations η \eta from the Hilbert space L 2 ​ ( B ) L^{2}(B) .

arxiv-2601-00111.title: A compellingly simple proof of the speed of sound for interacting bosons
arxiv-2601-00111.creator: J. Eisert
arxiv-2601-00111.description: Abstract On physical grounds, one expects locally interacting quantum many-body systems to feature a finite group velocity. This intuition is rigorously underpinned by Lieb-Robinson bounds that state that locally interacting Hamiltonians with finite-dimensional constituents on suitably regular lattices always exhibit such a finite group velocity. This also implies that causality is always respected by the dynamics of quantum lattice models.

pmc-11497038.title: Ruthenium Anchored Laser‐Induced Graphene as Binder‐Free and Free‐Standing Electrode for Selective Electrosynthesis of Ammonia from Nitrate
pmc-11497038.creator: Zekun Geng, Zhiliang Feng, Haoran Kong, Jiaqi Su, Kaiyan Zhang, Jiaxin Li, Xinzhi Sun, Xiaojuan Liu, Lei Ge, Panpan Gai, Feng Li
pmc-11497038.description: Developing effective electrocatalysts for the nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) is a promising alternative to conventional industrial ammonia (NH3) synthesis. Herein, starting from a flexible laser‐induced graphene (LIG) film with hierarchical and interconnected macroporous architecture, a binder‐free and free‐standing Ru‐modified LIG electrode (Ru‐LIG) is fabricated for electrocatalytic NO3RR via a facile electrodeposition method.

pmc-11548679.title: The Efficacy of Botulinum Toxin Type A (BTA) in the Treatment of Hypertrophic Scars and Keloids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmc-11548679.creator: Elshymaa E Raslan, Basel H Bakhamees, Tafe A Howsawi, Layan S Alshmrani, Araa G Alruwaili, Abdulrahman Y Alhashmi, Shatha M Aldor, Wiam M Alhoshani, Maryam Y Almuslem, Rana A Alharbi, Afaf H Homeirani, Sarah K Alkhorayef, Mohammed A Alqahtani
pmc-11548679.description: Hypertrophic scars cause significant physical and emotional discomfort. Botulinum toxin type A (BTA) has shown promising outcomes in reducing scar formation. Research suggested its effectiveness in managing hypertrophic scars and keloids. This systematic review and meta-analysis were reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, including randomized controlled trials (RCTs).

pmc-11678747.title: The Effect of Physiotherapy on Arthrogenic Muscle Inhibition After ACL Injury or Reconstruction: A Systematic Review
pmc-11678747.creator: Maria Paço, Maxence Peysson, Elona Dumont, Mário Correia, Anna Quialheiro, Paula Chaves
pmc-11678747.description: Arthrogenic muscle inhibition (AMI) following ACL injury or reconstruction is a common issue that affects muscle activation and functional recovery. Thus, the objective of this study was to systematize the literature on the effects of physiotherapy interventions in the rehabilitation of AMI after ACL injury or reconstruction. A systematic review was conducted following the PRISMA guidelines.

pmc-12608978.title: Unraveling the Burden of Viral and Bacterial Central Nervous System Infections: A Two-Year Retrospective Study
pmc-12608978.creator: Nabeel Alzahrani, Ahmed Alshehri, Ali Alshehri, Sameera Al Johani, Georgina Tzanakaki
pmc-12608978.description: Background/Objectives: Central nervous system (CNS) infections remain a significant public health challenge and require rapid and accurate diagnosis to guide clinical management. Although the incidence of bacterial meningitis has declined owing to widespread vaccination, viral etiologies continue to dominate CNS infections.

pmc-12626228.title: 1. Introduction

pmc-12626228.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). crashes and workplace accidents to violence and unintentional harm—continues to rise, yet remains a largely under-recognized public health epidemic. Compounding these risks are the rapid digital transformations reshaping our societies. The spread of artificial intelligence and digital connectivity has introduced new vectors of harm—from cyberviolence, particularly targeting women, to broader cybersecurity and data protection threats—demanding a forward-looking, equity-driven approach to health and safety. Responding to this landscape requires more than robust emergency preparedness.

pmc-12643856.title: How does mindful awareness impact academic performance in junior high school students? A chain mediation effect based on academic self-efficacy and academic buoyancy
pmc-12643856.creator: Jianwen Guo, Jiahao Zhang, Lei Qiao, Yun Zhou
pmc-12643856.description: BackgroundPrevious research has mostly focused on exploring the mechanisms of mindful awareness and academic performance in university students, with less attention paid to junior high school student group. This study aimed to examine how mindful awareness influences academic performance in junior high school students through the chain mediation of academic self-efficacy and buoyancy.

pmc-12935218.creator: Nancy Mugisha, Fanjalalaina Rasoanaivo, Mbolatiana Raza-Fanomezanjanahary, Fiainamirindra Anjaratiana Ralaivavikoa, Tanjaka Andriamanampy, Giovanna Cowley, Haja Ramamonjisoa, Claude Rakotonirina, Tojosoa Rajaonarison, Judith Rahanitriniaina, Mamy Andrianomenjanahary, Lalaina Narovananahary Rakotovoa
pmc-12935218.description: Diabetes is a significant cause of disabilities and deaths in Africa. In Madagascar, diabetes causes an estimated 5,000 deaths yearly. There are many barriers to diabetes care in Madagascar, and a key barrier is health systems readiness to provide care, especially in rural areas.

pmc-13116450.title: 10-epi-Protectin DX and Resolvin D5n-3 DPA Attenuate Multi-Organ Inflammatory Injury in an LPS-Induced Murine Endotoxemia Model
pmc-13116450.creator: Suyeon Kim, Uijin Kim, Nahyun Kim, Tae-Eui Lee, Jin Lee, Deok-Kun Oh, Ha Youn Shin
pmc-13116450.description: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome driven by dysregulated immune activation and multi-organ dysfunction, with limited effective therapies. Oxylipins are endogenous lipid mediators that promote the resolution of inflammation and tissue repair, yet their therapeutic potential in systemic inflammatory diseases remains incompletely understood.

pmc-13574388.title: Post-cannulation prognostic reassessment in ECPR
pmc-13574388.creator: Taekwon Kim, Sang-hun Lee, Kyungsub Song, Jonghoon Yoo
pmc-13574388.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Static prognostic scores for extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation have been developed for pre-cannulation risk estimation and are frequently repurposed for post-cannulation decisions, where early treatment response may be more informative. We evaluated 3 widely used pre extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) scores (TiPS65, RESCUE-in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA), and Survival After Veno-Arterial ECMO) for in-hospital mortality in a single-center cohort of 158 adults treated with extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (2015-2022).
